blocks.text: In Greengold functions are values too: you can store one in a variable, pass it as a parameter or put it in a struct field. A function type is written `fn(T1, T2) -> R`; since it is long it is often named with `type`.

code: fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32:
fn multiply(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32:
fn apply_op(op: MathOp, x: i32, y: i32) -> i32:

blocks.text: `apply_op` does not know which operation it will do; the function it is given decides. This is the basic way to pass behaviour as a parameter.

blocks.prompt: Write a `subtract` function and print the result of `apply_op(subtract, 10, 4)`.

blocks.q: What kind of type is `fn(i32, i32) -> i32`?
options: The type of functions taking two `i32` and returning `i32`
blocks.why: A function type describes the parameter and return types.
